title: Dance-hall job on Canal Street with Willie Paiso
summary: At the Alamo he played ticket dances with Paiso, choruses cut short, two to five choruses per number.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: At that time, that was the goal, you know, to make these bands and playing the orchestration. So I played with them a good while until I got a regular job on the canal in London. It was the Alamo we had there. I got a job there with Willie Paiso. Where did they play there? What kind of music? Jitney. Feet music? Or was it a hand cell? No, no. No, just didn't have time to fool with no music because you pick up number one behind the other, nothing but chorus. And people get there and dance. A man come in the place and buy a lot of tickets. That's a piece. You cut the numbers off short. Each dance was a ticket. They'd tear a ticket off from his role. Would you play one chorus or two chorus? I played two or three. Sometimes I played just two. Sometimes I played maybe four or five.
I played a lot. I'll give my break, huh? Mm-hmm. Well, did you enjoy playing from the arrangements more or playing just head arrangements?
